q: 'Playing It My Way' is the autobiography of:
e: Playing It My Way is the autobiography of cricketer Sachin Tendulkar, in which he recounts his 24-year international career.

q: The book 'Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind' was written by:
e: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind, the bestseller tracing the history of the human species, was written by Israeli historian Yuval Noah Harari.

q: The novel 'Animal Farm' was written by:
e: Animal Farm, the allegorical fable about farm animals revolting against their owner, was written by George Orwell.

q: The novel 'A Tale of Two Cities' was written by:
e: A Tale of Two Cities, set in London and Paris during the French Revolution, was written by the English novelist Charles Dickens.

q: The book 'Alice's Adventures in Wonderland' was written by:
e: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, featuring Alice and characters like the Cheshire Cat and the Mad Hatter, was written by Lewis Carroll.

q: The novel 'War and Peace' was written by:
e: War and Peace, the vast novel set against Napoleon's invasion of Russia, was written by the Russian author Leo Tolstoy.

q: The book 'The Argumentative Indian' was written by:
e: The Argumentative Indian, a collection of essays on Indian history, culture and identity, was written by Nobel laureate economist Amartya Sen.

q: 'My Story' is the autobiography of:
e: My Story is the frank autobiography of Malayalam writer Kamala Das, also known as Kamala Surayya and Madhavikutty.

q: The detective novel 'Murder on the Orient Express', set on a train, was written by:
e: Murder on the Orient Express, the Hercule Poirot detective novel set aboard a train, was written by Agatha Christie, the queen of crime fiction.

q: The railway-based children's book 'The Railway Children' was written by:
e: The Railway Children, the classic children's book about children living near a railway line, was written by Edith Nesbit.

q: The adventure novel 'Around the World in Eighty Days' was written by:
e: Around the World in Eighty Days, in which Phileas Fogg wagers he can circle the globe in 80 days, was written by French author Jules Verne.

q: The Sanskrit work 'Geet Govind' was composed by:
e: Geet Govind, the Sanskrit lyric poem on the love of Radha and Krishna, was composed by the 12th century poet Jayadeva.

q: The Railway Safety Review Committee (1998-99) was chaired by:
e: The Railway Safety Review Committee of 1998-99, set up after a series of accidents, was chaired by Justice H. R. Khanna.

q: The Expert Committee on Modernisation of Indian Railways (2011) was chaired by:
e: The Expert Committee on Modernisation of Indian Railways set up in 2011, which gave a five-year modernisation blueprint, was chaired by Sam Pitroda.

q: The National Transport Development Policy Committee, which submitted the India Transport Report, was chaired by:
e: The National Transport Development Policy Committee, which produced the India Transport Report on mobility for 2030, was chaired by Rakesh Mohan.

q: The Railway Accidents Committee of 1962 was chaired by:
e: The Railway Accidents Committee of 1962, which reviewed accident prevention on the railways, was chaired by Dr. H. N. Kunzru.

q: The Mandal Commission was appointed to:

options.A: Identify the socially and educationally backward classes in India
options.B: Examine the working of Centre-State relations
options.C: Recommend reforms of the electoral system
options.D: Review the safety record of Indian Railways

e: The Mandal Commission, chaired by B. P. Mandal, was appointed to identify the socially and educationally backward classes in India and recommend steps for their advancement.

q: The Kothari Commission (1964-66) was related to:
e: The Kothari Commission of 1964-66, chaired by Dr. D. S. Kothari, was an education commission whose report shaped the National Policy on Education 1968.

q: The Narasimham Committee (1991) is associated with reforms in the:
e: The Narasimham Committee of 1991, chaired by M. Narasimham, recommended wide-ranging reforms in the banking and financial sector, leading to banking sector liberalisation.

q: The Justice J. S. Verma Committee (2012-13) recommended amendments relating to:

options.D: Criminal laws concerning offences against women

e: The Justice J. S. Verma Committee of 2012-13 was set up after the Delhi gang rape case and recommended amendments to criminal laws relating to offences against women.

q: The inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India was recommended by the:
e: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment of 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

q: The Santhanam Committee (1962-64), on whose recommendation the Central Vigilance Commission was set up, dealt with:
e: The Santhanam Committee of 1962-64 dealt with prevention of corruption, and on its recommendation the Central Vigilance Commission was set up in 1964.

q: The National Commission on Farmers (2004) was chaired by:
e: The National Commission on Farmers, constituted in 2004, was chaired by Dr. M. S. Swaminathan, the architect of India's Green Revolution.

q: The Battle of Waterloo (1815) marked the final defeat of:
e: The Battle of Waterloo fought in 1815 in present-day Belgium marked the final defeat of French emperor Napoleon Bonaparte by the allied forces.

q: Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, was born at:
e: Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, was born in 1469 at Talwandi, a village now called Nankana Sahib in Pakistan.

q: India shares its longest land border with:
e: India shares its longest land border, about 4096 km, with Bangladesh, longer than its borders with China, Pakistan or Nepal.

q: Which is the largest ocean in the world?
e: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean in the world, covering more area than all the land surfaces of the Earth combined.

q: The Victoria Falls are located on the river:
e: The Victoria Falls, among the largest waterfalls in the world, are located on the Zambezi river on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe.

q: The practical incandescent electric lamp (bulb) is credited to:
e: The practical incandescent electric lamp is credited to Thomas Alva Edison, who developed a long-lasting bulb and the system for electric lighting.

q: Wireless telegraphy (radio) was developed by:
e: Wireless telegraphy, the basis of radio communication, was developed by Guglielmo Marconi, who sent the first transatlantic wireless signal.

q: The first successful powered aeroplane flight was made by:
e: The first successful powered and controlled aeroplane flight was made by the Wright brothers, Orville and Wilbur Wright, in 1903 at Kitty Hawk.

q: Insulin, used in the treatment of diabetes, was discovered by:
e: Insulin, the hormone used in treating diabetes, was discovered by Frederick Banting along with Charles Best, and the discovery was later developed at Toronto.

q: Radium was discovered by:
e: Radium was discovered by Marie Curie, together with her husband Pierre Curie, from the ore pitchblende in 1898.

q: A stethoscope is used by doctors to:

options.A: Listen to the sounds of the heart and lungs

e: A stethoscope is the acoustic instrument doctors place on the chest to listen to the internal sounds of the heart and lungs.

q: A periscope is used in a submarine to:

options.A: Measure the depth of the sea
options.B: See objects above the surface of the water
options.C: Detect other vessels by sound waves
options.D: Measure the speed of the submarine

e: A periscope in a submarine uses mirrors or prisms to let the crew see objects above the surface of the water while the submarine remains submerged.

q: An ammeter is an instrument used to measure:
e: An ammeter is connected in series in a circuit and measures the electric current flowing through it, in amperes.

q: An odometer in a vehicle measures:

options.A: The distance travelled by the vehicle
options.C: The fuel consumed by the vehicle

e: An odometer in a vehicle records and shows the total distance travelled by the vehicle.

q: A pyrometer is an instrument used to measure:
e: A pyrometer is a non-contact instrument used to measure very high temperatures, such as those inside furnaces, from the thermal radiation emitted.

q: The first woman to join the Indian Police Service (IPS) was:
e: Kiran Bedi, of the 1972 batch, was the first woman to join the Indian Police Service.

q: Who is popularly known as the 'Nightingale of India'?
e: Sarojini Naidu, the freedom fighter and poet, is popularly known as the Nightingale of India for her lyrical English poetry.

q: The Central Organisation for Modernisation of Workshops (COFMOW), which was dissolved with effect from 01.12.2022, was mainly responsible for:

options.A: Modernisation of railway stations across all zones
options.B: Recruitment of technical staff for workshops
options.C: Electrification of workshop sheds and colonies
options.D: Procurement of machinery and plant for railway workshops and production units

e: COFMOW was mainly responsible for selection and procurement of machinery and plant for railway workshops and production units. It was dissolved with effect from 01.12.2022 and its functions were transferred to zonal railways/production units and the Railway Board. (Source: Railway Board closure decision conveyed 18.10.2022; effective 01.12.2022).

q: The National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) is a joint venture of the Government of India with the State Governments of:
e: The National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited is a joint venture of the Government of India with the State Governments of Gujarat and Maharashtra, the two states through which the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor passes.

q: The corporate headquarters of the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) is located at:
e: The corporate headquarters of the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation, the catering and e-ticketing PSU, is located at New Delhi.

q: The corporate office of the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) is located at:
e: The corporate office of the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited is located at New Delhi.

q: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) is registered with the Reserve Bank of India as a:
e: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation is registered with the Reserve Bank of India as a Non-Banking Financial Company, in the infrastructure finance company category.

q: The Konkan Railway Corporation Limited was set up with equity participation of the Government of India and how many State Governments?
e: The Konkan Railway Corporation Limited was set up with equity participation of the Government of India and four State Governments - Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka and Kerala.

q: The head of the Railway Board is designated as the:

options.A: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Railway Board

e: Since the reorganisation of the Railway Board in 2020, its head is designated as the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Railway Board.

q: Braithwaite and Company Limited, a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Railways, is mainly engaged in the manufacture of:
e: Braithwaite and Company Limited, a PSU under the Ministry of Railways based in Kolkata, is mainly engaged in the manufacture of railway wagons.

q: The Kolkata Metro Rail Corporation (KMRC) was set up mainly to implement the:

options.C: Metro network of New Town, Kolkata

e: The Kolkata Metro Rail Corporation was set up as a special purpose vehicle mainly to implement the East-West Metro corridor of Kolkata, which passes under the Hooghly river.

q: The Container Corporation of India Limited (CONCOR) is categorised as a:
e: The Container Corporation of India Limited is categorised as a Navratna company, a status given to high-performing central public sector enterprises.

q: Rail Bhawan in New Delhi houses the:

options.A: Headquarters of the Ministry of Railways and the Railway Board

e: Rail Bhawan in New Delhi houses the headquarters of the Ministry of Railways and the Railway Board.

q: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) at Lucknow is headed by an officer designated as the:
e: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation at Lucknow, a directorate of the Ministry of Railways, is headed by an officer designated as the Director General.

q: The headquarters of Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) is located at:
e: The headquarters of Rail Vikas Nigam Limited, the infrastructure PSU of the Railways, is located at New Delhi.

q: The Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya (DDU) division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya division, earlier the Mughalsarai division, is a division of the East Central Railway headquartered at Hajipur.

q: The Bhavnagar division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Bhavnagar division, serving the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, is a part of the Western Railway.

q: The Jammu division, constituted in 2025, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Jammu division, inaugurated in January 2025 after being carved out mainly from the Firozpur division, functions under the Northern Railway.

q: The Liluah Carriage and Wagon Workshop of Eastern Railway is located in which district of West Bengal?
e: Liluah, where the Eastern Railway Carriage and Wagon Workshop is situated, lies in Howrah district of West Bengal.

q: The Jagadhri Workshop of Northern Railway, which undertakes overhaul of coaches and wagons, is located in which State?
e: Jagadhri, where the Northern Railway workshop undertaking overhaul of coaches and wagons is located, is in Yamunanagar district of Haryana.

q: The Kanchrapara Workshop, one of the oldest workshops of Indian Railways, belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Kanchrapara Workshop, one of the oldest workshops of Indian Railways established in 1863, belongs to the Eastern Railway.

q: The Kharagpur Workshop of South Eastern Railway is located in which State?
e: Kharagpur, where the South Eastern Railway workshop is located, is in Paschim Medinipur district of West Bengal.

q: The Golden Rock Railway Workshop at Tiruchirappalli is mainly engaged in:

options.D: Periodic overhaul of coaches and wagons and manufacture of wagons

e: The Golden Rock Railway Workshop at Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu is mainly engaged in periodic overhaul of coaches and wagons and in the manufacture of wagons.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Financial Management (IRIFM) at Secunderabad mainly imparts training to:

options.A: Probationers and officers of the railway accounts and finance service
options.B: Commercial clerks of all zonal railways
options.C: Loco pilots and assistant loco pilots

e: The Indian Railways Institute of Financial Management at Secunderabad mainly imparts training to probationers and officers of the railway accounts and finance service.

q: The electric locomotive factory at Madhepura in Bihar manufactures which high-power locomotive for Indian Railways?
e: The Madhepura electric locomotive factory manufactures the WAG-12 freight locomotive of 12000 HP, among the most powerful locomotives in India.

q: The Railway Museum at Mysuru, one of the earliest railway museums of India, is located in which State?
e: The Railway Museum at Mysuru, set up in 1979 as one of the earliest railway museums of India, is located in Karnataka.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'LHB', used for modern passenger coaches, stands for:
e: LHB stands for Linke Hofmann Busch, the German firm whose design is used for the modern, safer and faster passenger coaches built in India.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'IRCA' stands for:
e: IRCA stands for Indian Railway Conference Association, the body associated with rules for coaching and goods tariffs and inter-railway commercial matters.

q: In railway commercial working, the abbreviation 'EFT', a ticket issued by the ticket checking staff, stands for:
e: EFT stands for Excess Fare Ticket, the receipt-cum-ticket issued by ticket checking staff to passengers for excess fare, extension of journey or travelling without a proper ticket.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'HHT', the device used by ticket checking staff for checking reserved charts, stands for:
e: HHT stands for Hand Held Terminal, the device used by ticket checking staff on trains to check reserved charts and allot vacant berths electronically.

q: In railway accounts, the abbreviation 'DRF', a fund maintained for replacement and renewal of assets, stands for:
e: DRF stands for Depreciation Reserve Fund, the railway fund credited with depreciation charges and used for replacement and renewal of assets.

q: In the context of retirement benefits of railway employees, the abbreviation 'NPS' stands for:
e: NPS stands for National Pension System, the defined contribution pension system that covers railway employees recruited on or after 1 January 2004.

q: In Railway Recruitment Board examinations, the abbreviation 'NTPC' stands for:
e: In Railway Recruitment Board examinations, NTPC stands for Non-Technical Popular Categories, the undergraduate and graduate level posts for which a common exam is held.

q: In railway budgeting and financing, the abbreviation 'EBR' stands for:
e: EBR stands for Extra Budgetary Resources, the funds raised by the Railways outside the budget, such as market borrowings through IRFC and institutional finance, for capital works.

q: In railway stores purchases, the abbreviation 'PAC', used for procurement of proprietary items, stands for:
e: PAC stands for Proprietary Article Certificate, the certificate used in stores purchases to justify procurement of a proprietary item from a single source.

q: In railway workshops, the abbreviation 'POH', the comprehensive overhaul given to coaches and locomotives at fixed intervals, stands for:
e: POH stands for Periodic Overhaul, the comprehensive overhaul given to coaches, wagons and locomotives in workshops at fixed prescribed intervals.

q: In railway reservation, the abbreviation 'BPT', a ticket issued manually when computerised reservation is not available, stands for:
e: BPT stands for Blank Paper Ticket, the manually issued ticket used when computerised reservation is not available at a station.

q: The first Amrit Bharat Express, flagged off in December 2023, connects Darbhanga in Bihar with:

options.C: Anand Vihar Terminal, Delhi, via Ayodhya

e: The first Amrit Bharat Express, flagged off in December 2023, runs from Darbhanga in Bihar to Anand Vihar Terminal in Delhi via Ayodhya.

q: The first Vande Bharat Express service to Srinagar, started in June 2025 after completion of the USBRL project, was flagged off from:
e: The first Vande Bharat Express service to Srinagar, started in June 2025 after completion of the USBRL project, was flagged off from Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra.

q: The Ayodhya railway station of Uttar Pradesh was renamed in 2023 as:
e: Ayodhya railway station in Uttar Pradesh was renamed in 2023 as Ayodhya Dham Junction ahead of the consecration of the Ram temple.

q: The Bairabi-Sairang railway line, inaugurated in September 2025, brought rail connectivity close to Aizawl, the capital of:
e: The Bairabi-Sairang railway line, inaugurated in September 2025, brought rail connectivity close to Aizawl, the capital of Mizoram, making it the fourth north-eastern capital on the rail map.

q: India's first hydrogen-powered train has been introduced as a pilot project on which route of Northern Railway in Haryana?
e: India's first hydrogen-powered train has been developed as a pilot project on the Jind-Sonipat route of Northern Railway in Haryana, with a hydrogen plant at Jind.

q: Indian Railways has integrated its passenger enquiry and complaint services into a single helpline number, which is:
e: Indian Railways has integrated its enquiry and complaint services into the single helpline number 139, which also works through the Rail Madad system.

q: 'Operation Nanhe Farishtey' of the Railway Protection Force is an initiative for:

options.C: Saving the lives of passengers who fall from trains
options.D: Rescuing children in need of care and protection found at stations and in trains

e: Operation Nanhe Farishtey is an RPF initiative for rescuing children in need of care and protection who are found at railway stations and in trains, and handing them over to the proper authorities.

q: The Rail Kaushal Vikas Yojana of the Ministry of Railways mainly aims at:

options.A: Providing free rail travel to skilled workers
options.B: Recruiting apprentices directly into railway service
options.D: Imparting entry-level industry-relevant skill training to youth through railway training institutes

e: The Rail Kaushal Vikas Yojana aims at imparting entry-level, industry-relevant skill training to youth in various trades through railway training institutes, to improve their employability.

q: The first Vande Bharat Express of the North-East, flagged off in 2023, connects Guwahati with:
e: The first Vande Bharat Express of the North-East, flagged off in 2023, connects Guwahati in Assam with New Jalpaiguri in West Bengal.

q: The electrification of the entire Konkan Railway route was completed in the year:
e: The electrification of the entire Konkan Railway route, a 740 km long line along the west coast, was completed in 2022.

q: The book 'Malgudi Days' was written by:
e: Malgudi Days, the collection of short stories set in the fictional town of Malgudi, was written by R. K. Narayan.

q: The novel 'Anandamath' was written by:
e: Anandamath, the Bengali novel containing the song Vande Mataram, was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

q: The novel 'A Suitable Boy' was written by:
e: A Suitable Boy, one of the longest novels in English, set in post-independence India, was written by Vikram Seth.

q: The novel 'The Shadow Lines' was written by:
e: The Shadow Lines, the novel moving between India, Bangladesh and England across generations, was written by Amitav Ghosh.

q: The short story collection 'Interpreter of Maladies', which won the Pulitzer Prize, was written by:
e: Interpreter of Maladies, the short story collection by Jhumpa Lahiri on Indian and Indian-American lives, won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 2000.

q: The novel 'The Inheritance of Loss', which won the Booker Prize in 2006, was written by:
e: The Inheritance of Loss, set in Kalimpong and New York, was written by Kiran Desai and won the Booker Prize in 2006.

q: The book 'Hind Swaraj' (Indian Home Rule), written in 1909, was authored by:
e: Hind Swaraj, also called Indian Home Rule, was written by Mahatma Gandhi in 1909, setting out his ideas on swaraj and his critique of modern civilisation.

q: The novel 'Jane Eyre' was written by:
e: Jane Eyre, the story of the orphaned governess Jane Eyre, was written by Charlotte Bronte and published under the pen name Currer Bell.

q: The novel 'Wuthering Heights' was written by:
e: Wuthering Heights, the novel of Heathcliff and Catherine set on the Yorkshire moors, was written by Emily Bronte.

q: The famous Spanish novel 'Don Quixote' was written by:
e: Don Quixote, regarded as the first modern novel, was written by the Spanish author Miguel de Cervantes.

q: The novel 'Crime and Punishment' was written by:
e: Crime and Punishment, the novel about the student Raskolnikov who commits murder, was written by Russian author Fyodor Dostoevsky.

q: The novel 'Les Miserables' was written by:
e: Les Miserables, the epic novel centred on Jean Valjean and set in 19th century France, was written by Victor Hugo.

q: The adventure novel 'The Count of Monte Cristo' was written by:
e: The Count of Monte Cristo, the adventure novel of Edmond Dantes and his revenge, was written by French author Alexandre Dumas.

q: The adventure novel 'Treasure Island' was written by:
e: Treasure Island, the adventure novel about Jim Hawkins and the search for buried pirate treasure, was written by Robert Louis Stevenson.

q: The novel 'Robinson Crusoe' was written by:
e: Robinson Crusoe, the novel about a man shipwrecked and marooned on a desert island, was written by Daniel Defoe.
